title: Phones draw the far railway yard cheaper; elm leaves look real
items: On a phone, the Illinois Central yard's cinders, ballast and lake edge more than about 240 m away are drawn from a coarser copy of the same ground, with the same colours. Looking down Prairie Avenue from 18th Street that is about 11% less for the phone to draw, and about a quarter less on the lakeside. The yard looks the same, from the street and from the air. Desktop is unchanged.

The elms' leaves take their surface from a real American elm leaf: its veins and mottle, photographed by Steven J. Baskauf (Bioimages, Vanderbilt University, CC BY 4.0). Their shapes and their July colour are unchanged.
